Values are read only from the bank's own domain or a .gov domain during this session. Nothing is inferred; conflicting official pages are published as conflicts, not averaged.

new_flags.title: Axos's own page contradicts itself: the 5.00% headline does not appear anywhere in its published rate table
new_flags.detail: The Axos ONE page advertises 'up to 5.00% APY' for the first six months, and the live dashboards model 5.00% on the first $50,000. But the rate table printed further down the SAME page shows the BOOSTED rate for every tier from $0 to $249,999.99 as 4.12% interest / 4.21% APY, and 3.44% / 3.50% from $250,000 up. No tier on that table pays 5.00%. Modelling 5.00% on any portion of the balance therefore overstates the return relative to Axos's own tier table. Treat the Axos ranking on the primary dashboard as unconfirmed until Axos reconciles the two figures.

new_flags.title: Citi's promotional savings rate feature is discontinued the day after the modelled opening date
new_flags.detail: Citi's Simplified Banking Fact Sheet states: 'Effective October 23, 2026, Promotional Rate Feature for New Citi Savings accounts will be discontinued.' The reference opening date for this whole project is 2026-10-22 — one day earlier. Any Citi promotional savings figure is valid for a one-day window and should not be relied on.

new_flags.title: PNC publishes two different High Yield Savings APYs on its own domain
new_flags.detail: The PNC High Yield Savings page served at pnc.com carries the document title 'High Yield Savings Account | 3.15% Annual Percentage Yield APY', while the same page served with PNC's own affiliate tracking parameter carries '3.30% Annual Percentage Yield'. The rate is not rendered in the page body to an automated reader. Because two official PNC URLs disagree and neither prints an effective date in the body, the PNC APY is left BLANK here rather than resolved to either figure.

new_flags.title: Alto deposits are not separately insured from other BMO accounts, and Alto has no app or branch access
new_flags.detail: BMO states that deposits made through Alto and in other U.S. accounts under the BMO brand are not separately insured and count toward one FDIC limit at BMO Bank N.A. Alto also states its accounts cannot be serviced through BMO branches, BMO ATMs or BMO Digital Banking, and the official page names no Alto mobile app — relevant because a digital app is one of this project's stated requirements.

new_flags.title: Four separate brand pairs share a single FDIC certificate — a real risk to a max-coverage plan
new_flags.detail: Openbank + Santander Bank share Cert #29950. CIT Bank + First-Citizens Bank & Trust share Cert #11063. Alto + BMO Bank N.A. share Cert #16571. Barclays Tiered Savings + Barclays Online Savings + Select Savings (AARP) all share Cert #57203. Capital One 360 + the former Discover Bank share Cert #4297 (Discover's own Cert #5649 is inactive). Holding $250,000 at each brand in a pair does NOT produce $500,000 of coverage.

new_flags.title: Three banks cap the balance they will accept, below or near the amounts in the max-coverage tables
new_flags.detail: Marcus limits each Online Savings Account to $1,000,000 and each depositor to $3,000,000 across all Marcus deposit accounts. Barclays limits each Tiered Savings and each Select Savings account to $1,000,000, with a maximum of 3 such accounts. American Express sets a maximum account balance of five million dollars and allows no more than 20 accounts. These are bank product limits, not FDIC limits, and they constrain a single-bank concentration strategy.

new_flags.title: Wells Fargo's 3.25% is excluded in Colorado and is lost on any day the balance dips below $25,000
new_flags.detail: The Consumer Account Addenda scopes the Platinum Savings new-customer rate to 'All states excluding Colorado', and states that on any day the collected balance is below $25,000 the Standard or Relationship Interest Rate applies instead. The primary owner must also not have held any Wells Fargo consumer savings account in the previous 30 days.

new_flags.title: The FDIC trust category raises the single-bank ceiling to $1,250,000 — a fact absent from the published coverage tables
new_flags.detail: Since April 1, 2024 the FDIC insures trust accounts at $250,000 per eligible beneficiary up to five beneficiaries, for a maximum of $1,250,000 per owner per insured bank, covering both revocable (POD/ITF) and irrevocable trusts. The live dashboards' coverage tables show only the $250,000 single and $500,000 joint figures, which understates what one bank can insure for a depositor who uses the trust category.
